KV cache (short): we use a managed caching provider (EphemeralCache Co.) for inference KV storage; encryption-in-transit is TLS 1.3, keys are customer-isolated where required via our KMS integration (AWS KMS for hosted, customer-managed KMS for dedicated/private). Alex — attaching what we have prepared for ZenPort. See the summary below and links to the secure Drive folder.

Summary of deliverables included:
- redwood_subprocessor_manifest_2026-02.csv (attached) — current roster + onboarding column, data residency, KMS ownership field included.
- SOC2-summary-2025-redacted.pdf (attached) — high level scope, trust services criteria mapped, redactions limited to tenant IDs and ephemeral IPs.
- SIG-lite-evidence-2026-02.zip (Drive link) — includes CAIQ mapping, control narratives for KV cache, encryption diagrams, and a README with redaction guidance.

Key points / clarifications:
- KV cache vendor: EphemeralCache Co.; we operate the KV layer in a multi-tenant arrangement for hosted customers but support customer-isolated keying via AWS KMS when required. For Dedicated and Private deployments the KV cache can be run within customer VPCs under the customer's KMS.
- Keys: for hosted customers we manage envelope keys using our AWS KMS instances; customer-specific keys are supported on request (bring-your-own-KMS).
- Telemetry retention: metric/observability retention defaults: 90 days for aggregated metrics, 30 days for operational logs that include request IDs. Debug traces tied to support cases may be retained longer per incident SLA.
- Data movement: we do not send inference payloads to downstream analytics vendors by default; subprocessors that perform batch model training are explicitly listed in the manifest with transfer rationale and controls.
